External / portable drive · Accidentally formatted

Recover Files From a Formatted External Drive

A quick format erases the drive's table of contents but usually leaves your data in place, so recovery is often possible. A full format on Windows Vista or newer writes zeros over everything, and that data is gone for good.

2/5 · Low risk
Success odds: Varies

Scanning only reads the drive, but saving anything new onto it can overwrite what is left.

✋ Stop! Don't do this first

  • Do not copy any new files onto the formatted drive. New data overwrites what you want back.
  • Do not format it again, even to a different file system (a different way of organising files).
  • Do not install recovery software onto the formatted drive.

Your steps

0 of 6 done
  1. Show me how
    1. Think back: did the format finish in seconds or a few minutes? That was quick. Did it take hours? That was full.
    2. Windows: the Format window had a Quick Format tick box. Mac: Erase is normally quick unless you chose Security Options and moved the slider towards Most Secure.
    3. If you are not sure, carry on. Scanning is safe.
  2. Show me how
    1. Windows: click the USB icon in the taskbar, then Eject. Mac: click the eject button next to the drive in Finder.
    2. Do not set it up again for a new backup or file copy, even if a program asks.
  3. Show me how
    1. Plug it into a USB port on your computer, not through a hub, and leave it in its enclosure.
    2. Prepare a separate drive with enough free space for the results.
  4. Show me how
    1. Download TestDisk from cgsecurity.org to your computer's own drive and unzip it. Windows: run testdisk_win.exe as administrator. Linux live USB: sudo apt install testdisk, then sudo testdisk. Mac: brew install testdisk, then sudo testdisk.
    2. Choose Create, pick your external drive by its size, accept the partition type, then choose Analyse and Quick Search.
    3. If your old partition appears, press p to list its files and copy what you need with c to your other drive. Do not choose Write: it changes the drive itself.

    Guide: How to use TestDisk to copy files off a driveGuide: Data recovery glossary for beginners

  5. Show me how
    1. Run photorec_win.exe (Windows, as administrator) or sudo photorec (Mac or Linux, installed with TestDisk as above).
    2. Pick the external drive and the Whole disk line, choose Search, pick Other as the file system (unless it was a Linux drive) and Whole, then move to a folder on your other drive and press C.
    3. Expect hours for a large drive.

    Guide: How to use PhotoRec to recover photos and files

  6. Show me how
    1. Open a few of each type. Photos should show completely and documents should open without errors.
    2. If many files are blank or damaged, stop. Read the SSD guide if your drive has no moving parts.
Mission complete! 🎉 Check your recovered files open properly, then back them up in two places.

Questions people ask

Can I recover data after a full format?

On Windows Vista and later, no. A full format writes zeros over the drive. A quick format is often recoverable.

Did reformatting for a Mac or PC erase my files?

Reformatting to another file system counts as a format. If it was a quick format, the old data is just hidden. Stop using the drive and scan it right away.

Will I keep my folders?

Sometimes with TestDisk. With PhotoRec, files usually come back sorted by type with generic names.

Before you start: Educational DIY guide, no warranty. DIY recovery can cause permanent data loss. If the data is valuable, consider a professional first.
